title: Incident Response Plan Readiness Checklist
description: Checks an incident response plan against NIST SP 800-61r3 and the CSF 2.0 Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover outcomes most relevant to an IR plan. Each control lists concrete elements to look for in the document.
notes: Control IDs (IRP-xx) are this project's own. Only the CSF 2.0 Subcategory IDs and SP 800-61r3 table references are framework identifiers. Mapping a control to a Subcategory is a judgment by this project, not an official NIST crosswalk.

controls.title: The plan is formally approved and states its scope
look_for: Named approver or executive sponsor
Scope: which business units, systems and incident types it covers
Effective date or version
controls.sp800_61r3: SP 800-61r3 Section 3.1, Table 2 (Preparation and Lessons Learned)

controls.title: Incident response roles and responsibilities are defined
look_for: Named roles (for example incident lead, technical lead, communications, legal)
What each role does during an incident
Backups or deputies for key roles
controls.sp800_61r3: SP 800-61r3 Section 3.1, Table 2 (Preparation and Lessons Learned)

controls.title: Decision authority is assigned for high-impact actions
look_for: Who can declare an incident
Who can approve taking critical systems offline
Who decides on external notification and ransom or extortion demands
controls.sp800_61r3: SP 800-61r3 Section 3.1, Table 2 (Preparation and Lessons Learned)

controls.title: Incident declaration criteria are defined
look_for: Definition of an event versus an incident
Criteria or examples that trigger declaration

controls.title: A severity or prioritization matrix exists
look_for: Severity levels with definitions
Criteria such as business impact, data sensitivity or number of systems
Response time or actions per level

controls.title: Escalation paths and timelines are defined
look_for: Who is notified at each severity level
Time limits for escalation
After-hours escalation

controls.title: Incident reports are triaged and validated
look_for: How staff and tools report suspected incidents
Who triages reports and how they are validated

controls.title: Contact information for responders and third parties is maintained
look_for: Contact list for internal responders and leadership
External contacts such as legal counsel, forensics, insurer, law enforcement and key vendors
Out-of-band contact method if email or phones are compromised

controls.title: A communication plan covers internal and external stakeholders
look_for: Internal communication to staff and leadership
External communication to customers, partners and media
Who approves statements

controls.title: Legal and regulatory notification obligations are identified
look_for: Applicable notification laws, regulations or contracts
Deadlines and who is responsible for notifying

controls.title: The plan covers coordination with third parties
look_for: When and how to engage outside counsel, forensics firms or the insurer
Coordination with affected suppliers or service providers

controls.title: Evidence collection and preservation are defined
look_for: What evidence to collect (logs, images, memory)
Chain of custody or integrity protection
Retention of evidence

controls.title: Investigation and scoping steps are defined
look_for: How to determine what happened and the root cause
How to estimate the scope and magnitude of the incident

controls.title: Containment strategies are defined
look_for: Containment options such as isolating hosts, disabling accounts or blocking network traffic
Criteria for choosing a containment option and accepting its business impact

controls.title: Eradication steps are defined
look_for: Removing malware, attacker access and persistence
Resetting compromised credentials
Confirming eradication before recovery

controls.title: Recovery criteria and restoration priorities are defined
look_for: Criteria for starting recovery
Restoration priority of systems and services

controls.title: Backup integrity is verified before restoration
look_for: Backups are protected and tested
Backups are checked for integrity or compromise before restoring

controls.title: Restored systems are verified and the end of recovery is declared
look_for: Validation that restored systems are clean and working
Criteria and authority for declaring recovery complete
Completing incident documentation

controls.title: Recovery progress is communicated
look_for: Updates on recovery progress to internal and external stakeholders
Approved channels and messaging for public updates

controls.title: The plan is linked to business continuity and disaster recovery
look_for: Reference to BCP or DRP and when they are activated
Critical business functions and recovery objectives such as RTO or RPO
Manual or downtime procedures

controls.title: A post-incident review process is defined
look_for: Lessons learned meeting after incidents
Timeline and owners for improvement actions
controls.sp800_61r3: SP 800-61r3 Section 3.1, Table 2 (Preparation and Lessons Learned)

controls.title: The plan is tested through exercises
look_for: Tabletop or functional exercises
Frequency of testing
Improvements tracked from exercises
controls.sp800_61r3: SP 800-61r3 Section 3.1, Table 2 (Preparation and Lessons Learned)

controls.title: The plan is reviewed and updated on a schedule
look_for: Review frequency
Triggers for updates such as major incidents or organizational changes
Version history or document owner
controls.sp800_61r3: SP 800-61r3 Section 3.1, Table 2 (Preparation and Lessons Learned)
